regime_context: The detector shows a broad, crowded, metals-led tape: Silver Miners lead on momentum but are flagged 'fading' with zero breadth and a true crowding flag, while Gold Miners show the cleaner trend-health. Rotation breadth is wide (73% eligible) with no one-narrative structure and muted absorption (0.32), so there is no confirmed leadership handoff — this is a coexistence regime, not a rotation. Momentum rank is a focus lens only, and the one validated leg is the absolute-trend gate, which is helping on this market.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Silver Miners' leadership actually hands off to Gold Miners: the condition that would retire this watch is GDX sustaining a higher durability_bar than SIL for 10 consecutive trading days while SIL's breadth remains 0.0 and its val_state stays 'fading' — that would mark a confirmed metals-complex leadership handoff, not just a single-day cross.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Among the top-ranked metals complex, Gold Miners have the cleanest trend-health profile: eligible, hurst_tag 'trend', and a higher durability_bar (0.57) than Silver Miners (0.55, 'mixed', 'fading'). Silver leads on raw momentum but is crowded and fading; Gold's steadier trend-regime signal plus the market's validated absolute-trend gate supports staying with the more durable metals name rather than chasing the fading leader.
evidence: Gold Miners eligible=true, hurst_tag='trend', durability_bar=0.57 vs Silver Miners 0.55 'mixed'/'fading'
crowding_z=1.02 — moderately crowded but materially below Silver (1.52)
theses.dissent: The entire metals complex may be a reflexive, late-cycle inflation/geopolitics trade already extended; if gold consolidates and the macro narrative shifts back to AI tech (dominant macro theme n=66), trend-health signals alone offer no return edge and GDX could underperform.

falsifier.text: GDX loses its trend-gate eligibility (drops below its absolute trend) or lags SIL by 5% before the check-by date

theses.subject: Silver Miners
theses.thesis: Silver Miners top the momentum rank but carry three caution flags that argue against adding: crowded (z=1.52), val_state 'fading', and breadth=0.0 with no internal participation. The momentum rank is explicitly not a buy list, and chasing a fading, crowded, zero-breadth leader is the documented failure mode. 'Avoid' is a no-add call, not a fade.
evidence: breadth=0.0 — no internal participation behind the headline
guardrails.do_not_conclude: momentum rank is not a buy list; reflexivity means don't chase the crowded leader
theses.dissent: Silver can have violent, news-driven upside (geopolitics/monetary demand) precisely because it is concentrated and momentum-driven; avoiding it forfeits the strongest tape leader if the squeeze continues.

falsifier.text: SIL broadens out (breadth stays >0 over 5 days) and its durability_bar climbs back above Gold Miners while staying eligible

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Cybersecurity has the strongest trend-health composite outside of the crowded metals leaders: hurst_tag 'trend', the highest durability_bar in the eligible universe (0.61), and eligible under the validated absolute-trend gate. Its crowding (z=1.97) is high and argues for sizing down, not for avoiding. As a defensive-software exposure with genuine trend persistence, it offers a less-fading alternative to the metals concentration.
evidence: Cybersecurity durability_bar=0.61 (highest across eligible ranks), hurst_tag='trend'
eligible=true under the validated absolute-trend gate (gate_helps=true)
crowding_z=1.97 — crowded, so a sizing caution, not a reason to fade (per guardrails)
theses.dissent: Extreme crowding (z=1.97) in a rate-sensitive software name means it could de-rate sharply if the macro/policy backdrop turns hawkish; 'trend' health is coincident, not a return forecast, and CIBR has no forward edge from this detector.

falsifier.text: CIBR loses trend-gate eligibility or lags the S&P 500 by 5% before the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
